t: The Song Dynasty ruled China from 960 to 1279, governed by exam-selected scholar-officials rather than generals.
It ran the world's most commercial economy, with paper money and huge cities, and developed gunpowder weapons, the compass and movable type.
Lacking warhorses and cavalry, it lost the north to the Jurchen in 1127 and fell to Kublai Khan's Mongols after four decades of resistance.
dyk: Bi Sheng invented movable type using ceramic characters around 1040, some four centuries before Gutenberg's printing press.
ev: Zhao Kuangyin seizes power in the Chenqiao Mutiny and founds the Song Dynasty
The Chanyuan Treaty commits the Song to annual silk and silver payments to the Liao
Wang Anshi launches the New Policies to reform state finances
The Jurchen Jin capture Kaifeng and carry off emperors Huizong and Qinzong
Southern Song fleets defeat the Jin at Tangdao and Caishi
The Mongols begin the five-year siege of Xiangyang
Lin'an surrenders and the boy emperor Gong is taken north
The loyalist fleet is destroyed at Yamen, ending the Song Dynasty
